title: What's in a Package? Getting Visibility Into Dependencies Using Security-Sensitive API Calls
abstract: arXiv:2408.02846v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The Log4Shell vulnerability occurred because the JNDI (Java Naming and Directory Interface) lookup feature was used, even though it was not needed for log4j's core functionality. This case illustrates why developers may want visibility into the sensitive capabilities available through a dependency. The presence of a call alone does not establish that the call is unnecessary or risky. Security-sensitive APIs provide access to security-sensitive resources, such as filesystem, network, or process-related resources. If developers know which types of sensitive resources a dependency can access, they can control their dependencies at a finer grain, and they can consider an alternative dependency when a dependency makes unnecessary or suspicious security-sensitive API calls. translated_title: 包里有什么？通过安全敏感API调用实现对依赖项的可见性
translated_abstract: Log4Shell漏洞的发生是因为使用了JNDI（Java命名和目录接口）查找功能，尽管该功能对log4j的核心功能并非必需。这一案例说明了为什么开发人员可能希望了解依赖项所提供的敏感功能。但仅仅存在某个API调用，并不能确定该调用是不必要的或有风险的。安全敏感API提供对安全敏感资源的访问，例如文件系统、网络或与进程相关的资源。如果开发人员知道某个依赖项可以访问哪些类型的敏感资源，他们就可以更细粒度地控制其依赖项，并且当某个依赖项做出不必要或可疑的安全敏感API调用时，可以考虑使用替代的依赖项。然而，先前的工作尚未提供有文档记录、可重复的程序来推导特定生态系统的安全敏感API列表，因此开发人员缺乏系统性的方法……
tldr: 本文提出了一种有文档记录且可重复的方法，用于推导特定生态系统的安全敏感API列表，帮助开发人员了解依赖包可访问的敏感资源（如文件系统、网络、进程等），从而实现更细粒度的依赖控制和风险识别。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a documented, repeatable procedure for deriving ecosystem-specific security-sensitive API lists, enabling developers to gain visibility into which sensitive resources (e.g., filesystem, network, processes) their dependencies can access, for finer-grained dependency control and risk assessment.
